### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/data/:object (route, 67 pages)`
- **19** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9deb967b99bd93d010b747f5cbb078234a070b1a` — the merge of head `f8a821d054b102a3cb7885e0f54f2b08ddce8b55` into base `eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9deb967b99bd93d010b747f5cbb078234a070b1a && git checkout 9deb967b99bd93d010b747f5cbb078234a070b1a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e f8a821d054b102a3cb7885e0f54f2b08ddce8b55 && git checkout -B drift-repro eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e && git merge --no-ff f8a821d054b102a3cb7885e0f54f2b08ddce8b55

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eb20c33c456f4b9fdeafd0e7a5b5de274888848e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f8a821d054b102a3cb7885e0f54f2b08ddce8b55`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #15953 (body and all six comments, the classification table `6115219467`, the release premise `6114646323`, the claim `6115080386`, the two `os-dev-report`s `6115578862` / `6115950326`, and the seat's ACCEPT `6115991140` read as a claim to verify); PR #22907 (body, 10-file list, net diff against merge base `9fdb12752c`, +974 / −12); the 46 check-runs on this head, latest run per name. Judged against AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12 and Post-Task Checklist step 3. Nothing was built, run or re-run; `git show` / `git diff` / `git grep` on fetched refs and `gh api` reads only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Exports reachable — right.** `packages/verify/package.json` publishes one entry (`"."` → `dist/index.js` / `dist/index.d.ts`, CJS twins), and `src/index.ts` re-exports the five values (`runReferenceShapeProofs`, `deriveReferenceShapeCases`, `formatReferenceShapeReport`, `referenceShapeProbeValue`, `REFERENCE_SHAPE_PROBE_ID`) and nine types from `./reference-shape.js`. No subpath is needed. Build Core, the four Type Check jobs and Lint & Repo Gates are green on this head.
2. **Names and shapes coherent with the family — right.** `runReferenceShapeProofs(stack, token, config, options?)` sits beside `runCrudVerification(stack, token, config)` and `runRlsProofs(stack, adminToken, memberToken, config)`; `deriveReferenceShapeCases` beside `deriveCrudCases`; `formatReferenceShapeReport` beside `formatReport` / `formatRlsReport`; `ReferenceShapeReport` / `ReferenceShapeProofOptions` beside `VerifyReport` / `RlsReport` / `RlsProofOptions`. It parses the REST create answer the way `verify.ts:97` already does (`id ?? record.id`) and reads objects through the same `declaredCollection(config, 'objects')` as the CRUD family, so a multi-package artifact is covered.
3. **Nothing exported promises more than the implementation measures — right.** The claim in the changeset, README, `cli.mdx` and the docblocks is: every client-writable field whose type is in `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` (`lookup`, `master_detail`, `user`, `tree` — confirmed at `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts:154`), `readonly` and `system` fields excluded with the reason, three probes (boolean, number, embedded record; array elements when multi-valued), two doors, two operations, a refusal counted only when the engine names the probed field, `hardFailures = holes + failed`. The code does exactly that: `deriveReferenceShapeCases` excludes `system` / `readonly`, derives the probes and DROPS any the stored schema accepts (named in `droppedProbes`, never a hole); `runReferenceShapeProofs` iterates doors × operations × probes; `fieldStatus` maps admitted → `holes`, faulted → `failed`, unattributed or not-run → `inconclusive`, else `proven`; `summary.hardFailures` is `holes + failed`. Two notes, neither an over-claim: `cli.mdx` says "a field that admits one fails the run" and omits that a faulted door also counts (an under-statement; the README and changeset say both); `packages/verify/package.json`'s `description` still names two families (not a contract surface).
4. **`os verify --reference-shapes` — right.** `Flags.boolean`, `default: false`. With the flag, `runVerification` boots `bootStack(config, { multiTenant, hostRoot })` of its own inside try / finally `stop()`, adds `referenceShapes.summary.hardFailures` to the run's `hardFailures`, emits `referenceShapes` in the `--json` document and prints `formatReferenceShapeReport` on the text face. Without the flag, `referenceShapes` is `undefined`: `emitJson` is `JSON.stringify`, which drops the key; the text face prints only when set; the hard-failure sum adds `?? 0`. So no existing output, exit code or `--json` key moves. Pinned by `packages/cli/test/verify-reference-shapes.test.ts` (`'referenceShapes' in doc` is false, `hardFailures` 0, exit 0 without the flag) and by the `Dogfood Verify CLI` check, which runs `verify --rls` on the showcase without the new flag (`ci.yml:2180`) and is green on this head. The only change a flagless run can see is help text (the command description, one example, one flag).
5. **The verdict is the engine's, taken through the doors — right (PD #12).** REST: `stack.apiAs(token, 'POST' | 'PATCH', /data/...)`; system: `stack.hooks.run(object, op, input, { system: true })` (`handle.ts:730`, `namesSystem` at `:573`). The spec is read ONLY for the promise (`valueSchemaFor(field, 'stored').safeParse` to drop a probe the contract accepts) and never for the verdict; attribution reads the engine's own `fields[]` (`ValidationError.fields` at `record-validator.ts:240`; the REST `VALIDATION_FAILED` + `fields[]` envelope at `rest-server.ts:40` / `:765`). No `??` tolerance, no alias, no re-implemented shape rule. The attribution control (a stack double that refuses every write naming `name`) reads `inconclusive`, never `proven`.
6. **`CALLERS` row `not-a-served-read` for `packages/verify/src/reference-shape.ts` — true of the code.** The file calls `referenceTargetOf(def)` once, in `deriveReferenceShapeCases`. The answer lands in `ReferenceShapeCase.target` (a metadata name) and is used at `createdIds.get(c.target)` to pick the id its embedded-record probe carries; `createdIds` holds only ids of rows `buildBaseRecords` created through the REST door as the signed-in admin (`fillRelationalRefs` reads that map, writes nothing). When the target has no created row (a `user` field's `sys_user`) the constant `REFERENCE_SHAPE_PROBE_ID` is used. No record of the target is read, matched or served. The reason text matches; the pin's logic and the other sixteen rows are unchanged; Test Core (3/6) is green.
7. **Two `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows — true of the code.** The gate's candidate rule is an exported function whose parameter 0 is annotated with an interface declared in `packages/verify/src` and re-exported as a type from its index. `runReferenceShapeProofs(stack: VerifyStack, ...)` and `formatReferenceShapeReport(report: ReferenceShapeReport)` are candidates; `VerifyStack` is the concrete handle `bootStack` returns (no out-of-tree implementer) and `ReferenceShapeReport` is produced by this package — the same footing, and the same wording, as the `runRlsProofs` / `formatRlsReport` rows. `deriveReferenceShapeCases(config: any)` and `referenceShapeProbeValue(kind: ReferenceShapeProbeKind, ...)` (a union alias, not an interface) are not candidates. `VERIFY_STAND_IN_CHECKS` in `eslint.config.mjs` is untouched, so the guarded set is still the two driver stand-ins; the gate's reconciliation (both directions) passed in Lint & Repo Gates.
8. **Docs sentences against the diff — right.** README: "Three app-agnostic proof families"; the family bullet (types, probes, doors, operations, "refuse it naming the field"); the CLI example; the opt-in paragraph naming `multiple: true` `lookup` / `user` (the #22908 reading of `record-validator.ts`'s multi-value early return); the exit-code sentence (`holes` or `failed`) equals `hardFailures`; the programmatic snippet matches the signature; the status table matches `fieldStatus`; the API line matches `{ doors? }`. `cli.mdx`: the example line, the paragraph, and the `--json` key list (`referenceShapes` with `--reference-shapes`). All true of the diff; see item 3 for the one under-statement.
9. **Negative control and the card's ablation clause — met.** `reference-shape.test.ts` runs the same metadata under `OS_ALLOW_LAX_VALUE_SHAPES=1` on a stack of its own (a lax admission revokes the ADR-0104 attestation, so a shared stack would read wrong) → 3 fields with holes, `hardFailures` 3; through the CLI → exit 1, `hardFailures` 1. The engine-ablation at `777263207d` (marker in the built dist, test red, restore proven) is the dev's report, not re-run here.
10. **Classification table — acceptance bullet 1 met.** Comment `6115219467` was posted before any implementation; 14 rows, one per audit-named file (13) plus the ADR-0104 check; each D / R / K with destination, reason and residue. Row 14 is the family this slice lands. Rows for the next slices are recorded; the PR reads `Part of #15953`, so the card stays open.
11. **Scope and governance.** The ten paths touch no governed surface (Governed Surface Queue Guard green); the PR is draft, carries `needs:contract-review`, has zero submitted reviews. Check-runs on this head, latest per name: every job success; the skipped ones (`Auto Label`, `Check PR Size` on label-triggered re-runs, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`) are the expected-skip roster; `Check Changeset`'s latest run (01:12:25Z) completed success.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/verify`: minor — matches the diff.** Five new value exports and nine new types; nothing removed or renamed; the accept set widens. The card asks `minor` per new exported family: one family, one minor.
- **`@objectstack/cli`: minor — the level the `os verify` change measures.** A new opt-in flag and a new optional `--json` key; no existing flag, key or exit code moves (①.4). Not patch (a feature, not a fix); not major (nothing narrows).
- **`Clause-②` carriers agree and each is legal.** PR body line 2: `Clause-②: yes`. Changeset body: `Clause-②: yes`. Claim comment `6115080386`: `Clause-②: yes` (the bare form a claim line takes). `yes` with no arm is a legal declaration; `yes` takes at least `minor` and both bumps are `minor`; no `(narrowing)` arm, so this is not a breaking changeset and no migration text or ADR-0087 disposition is owed (the dev's `check-adr-0087-registration` run reads "adds no declared-breaking changeset"; `Check Changeset` is success on this head). The frontmatter matches the sibling dialect. The changeset cites #22908 for why the flag is opt-in.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Report `6115578862` (slice), six deviations:**
1. `--reference-shapes` opt-in rather than default → open question 1. Answered by the seat: A for now, with #22908 filed (open, `bug`, `priority:p2`, `domain:engine`, `pm:queue`), which records the dev's recommendation B for the PR that lands the engine repair. The changeset, README and `cli.mdx` say why. Closed.
2. `os verify` not run end to end against hotcrm (this tree is protocol 18, hotcrm pins `^17.7.0`; stage 1 refuses 118 `expression-invalid`; `bootStack` refuses the package). The family was run over hotcrm's shipped artifact on hotcrm's pinned engine (REST door) and on this tree's engine (both doors, migrated snapshot): 0 holes, 0 contradictions with the retired pin. **Escalated as a note for the card, not a FAIL reason:** the card's acceptance bullet 2 reads "runs from `os verify` on hotcrm's metadata", which cannot be met on this tree until hotcrm moves to protocol 18; the substitute evidence is the dev's report and is not reproducible from this review's inputs. The shipped controls (①.9) carry the family's correctness on their own; the epic PM reads that acceptance clause as met in substance when the card closes.
3. Not merged with `origin/main` — the queue merges; not a flag.
4. Docs outside the claimed surface → open question 2. Answered A: the README and `cli.mdx` paragraphs are in this PR, cross-lane declared on #6023. Closed.
5. Commit trailers follow AGENTS.md's model-free pair rather than the harness reminder — the repo's instruction outranks the reminder; not a contract matter.
6. Local leftovers (the read-only hotcrm clone, `/build1.pid`) — for a person, outside every repository; the seat's ACCEPT carries it under "For a person".

**Report `6115950326` (patch round), five deviations:** (1) the surface breach on `scripts/check-verify-stand-in-erasure.mjs` — ratified by the claim's edit (`6115080386`, "Widened by edit before the ACCEPT (ratified, not ordered)"), cross-lane declared on #6017, the gate's own prescribed remedy, two rows and no logic (①.7). Closed. (2) One PR-body patch — allowed that round. (3)–(5) restate the above. `open_questions`: none.

**Out-of-scope findings:**
- Report 1 #1 (the engine admits wrong-shaped elements on a `multiple: true` `lookup` / `user`) → filed by the seat as #22908, with the seam, the control and a named real producer (`app-showcase` `team_members`). Right under PD #10.
- Report 1 #2 (carrier none: fields read `inconclusive` where the CRUD-synthesized base record cannot satisfy an app's own rules) → noted in the PR body, not filed. Right under PD #10: a derivation limit reported per field and never counted as proven, not a defect.
- Report 2 #1 (`dispatch-gates` derives neither `check:verify-stand-in` for a `packages/verify/src` export change nor the `@objectstack/core` `repo` whole-tree pin; both reds were learned from CI) → the seat's ACCEPT defers it: "To file at the next fire", this fire's quota spent. **Escalated: not yet filed.** It is a reproducible tooling defect under PD #10 and the seat owes that card; it is not a reason to hold this PR.
